description: FIND-204's fix specifies `adjustBalancesForOutstandingDebt({citizens, loanRows}) -> citizens[]` as a pure, zero-I/O function that 'runs AFTER filterProductiveCitizens's own output and BEFORE computeColonySurplusUsd's own max(0, balance_i - perCitizenReserveUsd) step... the debt is subtracted from the citizen's OWN balance FIRST' (behavioral-spec.md lines 1246-1250; nearly identical language at lines 111-114). This composition-point description is INCOMPLETE against anicca-agent-spawn's CURRENT (freshly re-read this session) REQ-101, which specifies a THREE-step pipeline, not the two-step pipeline the lending spec's own composition text implies: (1) filterProductiveCitizens({citizens, ledgerRows, nowMs, bootstrapWindowDays}) -- filters the citizen array by ledger lifecycle status; produces NO balance field on any citizen record. (2) readCitizenBalances({citizens}) (~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/colony-balances.mjs) -- a NEW, EFFECTFUL, coordinator-run step that queries each citizen's balance directly from public chain RPC and is the ONLY place a balance_i figure is ever attached to a citizen record (anicca-agent-spawn behavioral-spec.md lines 296-309: 'computeColonySurplusUsd(...) then runs ONLY on filterProductiveCitizens's OUTPUT... where balance_i is that citizen's own most-recently-read liquid balance, obtained via a NEW, coordinator-run, registry-driven effectful step, readCitizenBalances({citizens})'). (3) computeColonySurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd}) -- consumes the NOW-balance-attached citizens array. Because adjustBalancesForOutstandingDebt is asserted to be pure/zero-I/O and must reduce an ALREADY-PRESENT balance figure ('the citizen's OWN already-resolved liquid-balance figure', line 1229), it can ONLY function correctly if inserted AFTER step (2), readCitizenBalances -- never between step (1) and step (2), where no balance field exists yet on any citizen record to adjust. The lending spec's own composition text, both in the Dependencies section and in REQ-109's own body, states the insertion point ONLY as 'AFTER filterProductiveCitizens's own output and BEFORE computeColonySurplusUsd' and NEVER mentions readCitizenBalances at all anywhere in either specs/behavioral-spec.md or specs/verification-architecture.md (confirmed via a full-document grep this session, zero matches for 'readCitizenBalances' in both files). An implementer following this feature's own literal, complete textual description of the composition point -- which never names the balance-fetching step at all -- has a real, concrete chance of inserting adjustBalancesForOutstandingDebt in the WRONG slot (immediately after filterProductiveCitizens, before readCitizenBalances runs), where every citizen record it receives has no balance field to reduce at all, silently defeating the entire fix FIND-204 was meant to deliver, or requiring the implementer to independently re-derive the correct ordering from the sibling spec themselves (which REQ-113 does mandate a fresh read of, but REQ-113's own re-read discipline is about citing iteration numbers/FIND-lists/gate-verdicts as durable facts -- it does not cover this specific structural gap in describing the composition point itself, which is a defect in THIS document's own text, not merely a staleness-of-citation issue).

evidence.snippet: This composition runs AFTER filterProductiveCitizens's own output and BEFORE computeColonySurplusUsd's own max(0, balance_i - perCitizenReserveUsd) step -- the debt is subtracted from the citizen's OWN balance FIRST, and computeColonySurplusUsd then applies its own reserve subtraction on TOP of that already-adjusted figure.

crossCheck.note: computeColonySurplusUsd({citizens, perCitizenReserveUsd}) then runs ONLY on filterProductiveCitizens's OUTPUT -- never on the raw registry array -- where balance_i is that citizen's own most-recently-read liquid balance, obtained via a NEW, coordinator-run, registry-driven effectful step, readCitizenBalances({citizens}) (~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/colony-balances.mjs), that queries EACH citizen's balance directly from PUBLIC CHAIN RPC. This confirms a THIRD, effectful, balance-attaching step sits between filterProductiveCitizens and computeColonySurplusUsd -- a step the lending spec's own composition-point description never names anywhere. Grep confirms zero occurrences of 'readCitizenBalances' in anicca-agent-lending/specs/behavioral-spec.md or specs/verification-architecture.md.
